data.title: Butterfield Announces Pricing of Registered Offering of $600,000,000 8.363% Fixed to Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2036
data.description:
The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited (“Butterfield”) ( | BSX: NTB.BH) today announced the pricing of a registered offering of $600 million aggregate principal amount of Butterfield’s 8.363% Fixed to Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2036.

Butterfield intends to use the net proceeds from this offering to finance a portion of the cash consideration and related fees and expenses for its proposed acquisition of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce’s approximately 91.7% interest in CIBC Caribbean Bank Limited and for general corporate purposes.

The offering is expected to close on or about November 25, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.

data.title: Steadright Signs Facilitator Agreement To Negotiate Critical Minerals Deal In Morocco
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Muskoka, Ontario – November 19th, 2026 – TheNewswire – Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (CSE: SCM) (“Steadright” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that it has entered into a Share Acquisition Facilitation and Funding Agreement dated November 13, 2026 (the “Agreement”) with Terracasa Investment & Consulting FZCO (“Terracasa”), a free zone company based in Dubai Silicon Oasis, United Arab Emirates. Under the Agreement, the Company will fund the acquisition of a 20% interest in a private Moroccan company that holds a critical minerals project in southern Morocco. The transaction would add a further asset to Steadright’s growing Moroccan portfolio, which includes interests in the TitanBeach Titanium Project and the Copper Valley Project, as well as a binding MOU for the historic Polymetallic Goundafa Mine.

The Transaction

Terracasa is acting as facilitator for the transaction, drawing on its prior dealings with the target company’s shareholders, from whom the 20% interest is being acquired. Under the Agreement, Steadright will provide the equivalent of CAD 400,000 to fund the acquisition, which will be paid from the Company’s existing cash. The shares are to be registered in the name of NSM Capital Sarl (“NSM”), a Moroccan company owned by Steadright (76.5%) and Critical Foundation Metals Inc. (“CFM”) (23.5%), giving Steadright an effective indirect interest of approximately 15.3% in the target company. The transaction is expected to complete within 30 days, or less. The identities of the target company and the project are being kept confidential at this stage for commercial reasons. The Company expects to provide further details upon completion of the transaction.

Role of the Facilitator

Terracasa will manage the remaining formalities for the acquisition, including coordinating with the Moroccan authorities and the target company’s shareholders to complete registration of the shares in the name of NSM. Terracasa will also provide Steadright with copies of the signed transfer documents, shareholder consents and the updated share register, and will report to the Company in writing every seven days until completion.

Related Party Disclosure

The CEO of Steadright holds an indirect interest of 6% in CFM through a 33% ownership interest in a private entity that owns 18% of the common shares of CFM. In addition, a consultant to the Company, who is the spouse of a former director of Steadright, together with her immediate family, is the controlling shareholder of CFM and owns a majority of CFM common shares.

ABOUT STEADRIGHT CRITICAL MINERALS INC.

Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. is a mineral exploration company established in 2019.

Steadright is focused on acquiring exploration and historical mining projects in the Moroccan critical minerals space that can be advanced toward production.

Steadright currently holds its Moroccan exposure through NSM Capital Sarl, which has a 32% interest in Shang Tang, a Moroccan-based company with over 192 sq. km of mineral exploration claims comprising the TitanBeach Titanium Project, along with the Copper Valley Project. Steadright also has a binding MOU for the historic Goundafa Mine in the Kingdom of Morocco, which is fully permitted for mining operations.

data.title: Bausch + Lomb post-surgical ocular pain asset fails phase 2 main goal
data.description:
Key points:
  • BL1332, a candidate for post-surgical ocular pain from Bausch + Lomb , failed to meet its primary endpoint in a phase 2 trial.
  • At 24 hours, the topical TRPV1 antagonist did not show a statistically significant improvement vs. vehicle in the sum of pain intensity differences in both dose strengths tested (0.30% and 0.15%).
  • Also, a secondary endpoint measuring pain reduction during the first six hours after surgery, the 0.30% dose demonstrated a nominally significant reduction compared to vehicle.
  • "These findings, together with results from a previously reported Phase 1b study of BL1332 in participants with capsaicin-induced pain, will help shape discussions with the FDA and the program's future development," the company said. 
  • The phase 2 trial was evaluating BL1332 in patients with pain after photorefractive keratectomy surgery.

data.title: P&G to Cut Up to 30% of Product-Supply Workers Amid Automation Push
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Procter & Gamble said it plans to cut 20% to 30% of its product-supply jobs by 2030, as it implements more automation into its supply chain.

The consumer goods company said the job cuts, which will include contractors, are part of its ongoing effort to lower supply-chain costs.

P&G expects to deliver $1.8 billion in annual productivity savings by the end of this decade, in part from the workforce reduction, Chief Product Supply Officer Luc Reynaert said during an investor day event Thursday.

Product supply is also becoming more automated, Reynaert said. "Success heavily depends on a workforce with the skills to scale and optimize these technologies," he said.

P&G has been working for several years to improve its supply chain through a program it calls Supply 3.0. The plan involves keeping supply steady, digitizing and automating the supply chain, training its workforce on those new tools, and improving sustainability.

Eventually, P&G is aiming for 90% or greater free cash flow productivity from the improvements.

"Supply 3.0 is not a destination. It is the foundation that will evolve us into the supply chain of the future," Reynaert said.

P&G didn't immediately respond to a request for comment about the job cuts.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Gap cuts forecast, but signs of Old Navy recovery lift shares
data.description:
By Neil J Kanatt and Danielle Kaye

Gap cut its annual sales and profit forecasts on Thursday after a slower-than-expected start to the holiday quarter, even as improving trends at Old Navy, its largest brand, signaled its turnaround efforts were gaining traction.

Shares of the US apparel retailer rose more than 2% in extended trading after Old Navy posted better-than-expected quarterly sales and the company named Vuori executive Ashley Kechter to lead Athleta, its struggling activewear brand.

Investors have been seeking signs that Old Navy is recovering from a recent slump. While the namesake Gap brand has driven recent growth, the rest of Gap's portfolio — encompassing Old Navy, Athleta and Banana Republic — has lagged.

Gap earlier this year blamed weak sales of dresses and other seasonal categories on merchandising missteps at Old Navy and appointed retail veteran Michael Francis as the banner's chief executive in August.

Old Navy's revenue rose 1% to $2.30 billion in the third quarter, beating analysts' expectations. Gap Chief Executive Richard Dickson said in a statement the banner showed "meaningful sequential improvement."

Gap now expects fiscal 2026 sales to be roughly flat, compared with its previous forecast for growth of 1% to 1.5%. Analysts on average had expected growth of 1.4%, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company lowered its adjusted annual earnings forecast to between $2.29 and $2.34 per share from its prior range of $2.35 to $2.45.

Athleta, Gap's smallest banner by revenue, continues to face pressure as it works through excess inventory and seeks to boost brand desirability. It reported a 15% drop in comparable sales in the third quarter.

For the holiday quarter, the retailer expects sales to range from flat to down 1%, compared with analysts' expectations for a 2.6% increase. The company said the current quarter started slowly before improving in recent weeks.

TJX said this week that holiday demand for discounted merchandise remained strong, but Target reported continued weakness in apparel, particularly in women's fashion.

For the third quarter ended October 31, Gap reported net sales of $4.01 billion, compared with analysts' average estimate of about $4.02 billion, while adjusted earnings per share of 82 cents beat expectations of 78 cents.

data.title: Bausch + Lomb's eye-drop drug fails to reduce pain after laser surgery in trial
data.description:
Bausch + Lomb , said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study.

However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing.

The contact lens maker said it plans to discuss the results with the US Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial.

Here are some details:

  • The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy, or PRK, a laser procedure used to correct vision

  • US-listed shares of the eye-care company were down 1.4% in extended trading

  • Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases, and there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways, the company said

  • At six hours after surgery, secondary goal of complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two BL1332 doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving placebo

  • The company also said patients treated with BL1332 showed signs of faster healing of the cornea, the eye's outer surface

(22:24 GMT) Sims Upgrades 1H SLS Earnings Estimate, Issues Group Guidance

By Rhiannon Hoyle

Sims raised its forecast for first-half earnings from its e-waste and data-center services business, citing new opportunities amid shortages of some data center components.

The company also issued first-half group-wide earnings guidance for the first time.

In prepared remarks for an annual shareholder meeting, Sims Chief Executive Stephen Mikkelsen said the company now expects first-half underlying earnings before interest and taxes of between 120 million Australian dollars, equivalent to US$79.9 million, and A$130 million from its Sims Lifecycle Services business, or SLS.

The outlook is up from a forecast of between A$75 million and A$90 million in August.

"Ongoing shortages of certain data center components have contributed to delays in construction and decommissioning," said Mikkelsen. "At the same time, customers are adapting to these shortages as they work to meet growing demand for AI. That shift has recently opened up new profit opportunities for SLS."

Sims expects first-half group underlying Ebit of between A$270 million and A$285 million, he said.

data.title: NextDC Tightens Funding Rules After Costly Data-Center Delay
data.description:
By Stuart Condie

SYDNEY--Australia's NextDC paused work on six data-center developments and tightened its rules for committing new funding to projects as it seeks to avoid a repeat of the problems that wiped more than 40% off the company's share price.

ASX-listed NextDC on Friday said it had paused capital commitments for five Australian centers and one in New Zealand, where planned capacity had yet to be contracted to customers.

The data-center operator said new rules for committing capital to development projects included waiting for necessary power supplies and planning approvals to be locked in.

Last month, NextDC's stock tumbled 42% to a nearly nine-year low after it abandoned the timeline for an expansion of one of its Melbourne facilities. The local electricity distributor had suspended necessary power-line upgrades safety concerns and opposition from local residents.

With NextDC unable to deliver capacity that had already been contracted to a large customer, it slashed its guidance and sparked worries among analysts over how it would fund other developments.

On Friday, NextDC said its rules for committing capital would also include a project having customer contracts, expected returns above cost of capital, and funding in place.

After completing the capital-expenditure review it announced last month, NextDC said it was mostly committed to delivering the contracted capacity in its forward order book.

It said it would prioritize contracted capacity at centers including M2 Melbourne, M3 Melbourne, KL1 Kuala Lumpur and S4 Sydney. It said it was considering a joint-venture structure for the latter campus as part of efforts to recycle capital.

Write to Stuart Condie at stuart.condie@wsj.com

data.title: ComEd Recognized as Most Reliable Power Grid in the U.S. With 2026 ReliabilityOne® Awards
data.description:
ComEd customers are served by the most reliable electric utility in the nation. PA Consulting yesterday presented ComEd with its 2026 ReliabilityOne® National Reliability Award, Outstanding Reliability Performance in the Midwest Region and the Grid Flexibility Awards. ComEd previously won the award in 2023.

"Being named the most reliable electric utility in the country is a credit to the dedication of our ComEd workforce and a demonstration of the value of the targeted investments we have made in our grid over the past decade,” said ComEd President and CEO Gil Quiniones. “Our proposed grid plan charts a path for continuing to deliver nation-leading reliability, while keeping affordability top of mind, even in a future with more extreme weather events and unprecedented growth in power demand. We believe that reliability should not come at the expense of affordability, and we are working hard to keep customer bills as low as possible."

The recognition comes as northern Illinois faces new pressures on its power grid. Families and businesses are using more electricity than ever as homes, vehicles and buildings go electric, and severe storms are becoming more frequent and intense. That’s why ComEd’s Grid Plan which will be decided upon in December, is designed to protect the reliability customers count on today and prepare the grid for the decades ahead.

“Congratulations to ComEd on this national recognition, reinforcing Illinois’ nation-leading position in electric reliability,” said Governor JB Pritzker. “As energy demands continue to grow, we remain focused on strengthening our electric grid, lowering costs for working families and businesses, and building a cleaner, more reliable energy future for all Illinoisans.”

Since ComEd began its smart grid investments in 2012, those upgrades have helped customers avoid nearly 27 million power interruptions and more than $5 billion in outage-related costs. Overall reliability, measured by how long customers are without power, has improved by more than 75 percent compared with the 2007–2011 average. Outages lasting 12 hours or more have fallen 69 percent over the same period. These investments include smart switches that automatically reroute power, stronger poles and wires, modernized substations and better storm preparedness. Together, they have also sped up recovery after severe weather. In 2025, ComEd restored power to half of customers affected by storms within two hours and 98 percent within 24 hours. Had it not been for grid investments, an additional 2.6 million customers would have lost power.

“Reliable energy infrastructure is essential to Illinois’ ability to attract investment, support businesses, and create jobs,” said Illinois Economic Development Corporation President and CEO Christy George. “ComEd is an important partner in that work, and this national recognition underscores the strength of our state’s energy infrastructure."

A recent study by ComEd and Argonne National Laboratories projects that the number of heavy rainfall events, as well as more instances of severe weather, in northern Illinois, defined as those producing more than two inches of precipitation, could nearly double by mid-century. To prepare, ComEd is already bringing more durable technologies to the grid like fibreglass poles and elevated substations, developing management strategies to address severe storms, warmer temperatures, invasive pests and tree health risks that can affect vegetation near power lines and planning for new environmental threats that could affect utility equipment and infrastructure.

Severe weather data helps inform grid investments, including ComEd’s latest multiyear grid plan, filed in January, that builds upon its previous plan to strengthen the grid, continue delivering safe and affordable electric service as well as nation-leading reliability for ComEd’s customers amid the challenges of increasingly extreme weather and rising energy demands. The plan aligns with the state’s clean energy and economic development growth goals reflected in the Illinois Climate and Equitable Jobs Act (CEJA) and the Clean and Reliable Grid Affordability Act (CRGA).

Grid Flexibility Award

ComEd also received the ReliabilityOne® Grid Flexibility Award which is presented to a ReliabilityOne® recipient that demonstrated a dedicated focus on providing its customers and grid users with means to cost effectively use the grid to meet their needs. ComEd demonstrated the ability to interconnect a variety of distribution energy resources as well as the ability to monitor and control their outputs to maintain safe, reliable and resilient power throughout the year. These flexible interconnections have been used to defer system upgrades, helping customers get additional value from existing infrastructure investments and enabling clean energy to be added to the system as cost effectively as possible.

ComEd expects to connect approximately 400 community solar projects by the end of 2026 with a little over 320 interconnected year-to-date. Approximately 500 community solar sites are currently within ComEd’s construction interconnection queue, and more than 500 additional projects are currently in the study phase of interconnection to assess system impact. As of October, approximately 8 gigawatts (GW) of renewable generation are interconnected within the ComEd zone, including 6 GW of utility-scale renewable generation and 2 GW of distributed generation resources. Increasing the supply of solar on the grid is critical to meeting the rising energy demands of Illinois.

All utilities operating electric delivery systems in North America are eligible for consideration for the ReliabilityOne® Award. This year we recognize six leading utilities in their respective regions, which include utilities from the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, Upper Midwest, Southeast, and Pacific Regions. The selection of provisional recipients is based primarily on system reliability statistics that measure the frequency (SAIFI) and duration of customer outages (SAIDI and CAIDI). After provisional recipients are selected, each company undergoes a rigorous certification process which provides an independent review and confirmation of the policies, processes and systems used to collect, analyze and report a company's reliability results. Additional awards are recognized based on analysis of certification findings.

About ComEd

ComEd is a unit of Chicago-based Exelon Corporation (), a Fortune 200 company and one of the nation’s largest utility companies, serving more than 10.7 million electricity and natural gas customers. ComEd powers the lives of more than 4 million customers across northern Illinois, or 70 percent of the state's population. For more information visit ComEd.com, and connect with the company on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, and YouTube.

About PA Consulting

PA Consulting believes in the power of ingenuity to build a positive human future. As strategies, technologies and innovation collide, we create opportunity from complexity. Our diverse teams combine deep expertise, innovative thinking and breakthrough technologies to help clients adapt, transform and achieve enduring results across consumer and manufacturing, defense and security, energy and utilities, financial services, government and public services, health and life sciences, and transport. As a Jacobs company, we combine strategic advisory, design and delivery as a single partner across the full program lifecycle. Together, our global team of approximately 47,000 help clients shape investment decisions, solve complex challenges and deliver lasting outcomes. Discover more at paconsulting.com and connect with PA on LinkedIn and X. PA. Bringing Ingenuity to Life.

PA Consulting’s ReliabilityOne® Awards are presented to electric utilities providing their customers with the highest levels of reliability in the industry. PA Consulting’s ReliabilityOne® study is based on standard industry reliability statistics that measure the frequency and duration of electric power outages. As a group, customers of ReliabilityOne® participants on average experienced over 56% fewer sustained outages, and their collective system saw 64% shorter outage durations than the average US investor-owned utility. PA Consulting has been analyzing electric utility performance since 1987. For more information, about PA Consulting, visit https://www.paconsulting.com/industries/energy-and-utilities
